name: Start seeds indoors
blurb: A packet of seeds costs less than one plant and gives you fifty. The failure points are few and all avoidable: sowing depth, light, and hardening off.
gear: Seed trays or module cells with drainage
Seed compost, which is lower in nutrients than potting compost
A bright windowsill or a grow light
steps: Read the packet for timing and sow accordingly; sowing too early gives you leggy plants with nowhere to go.
Sow at the right depth — roughly twice the seed’s diameter — and press small seeds onto the surface rather than burying them.
Water from below by standing trays in water, so you do not wash the seeds around.
Give them the brightest light you have the moment they germinate. Warmth germinates; light is what stops them stretching.
Prick out into individual pots once the first true leaves appear, handling by the leaf, never the stem.
Harden off over a week or two — increasing outdoor exposure — before planting out. Skipping this kills healthy plants in a day.
tips: Long pale stretched seedlings mean insufficient light. They rarely recover.
Damping off — seedlings collapsing at soil level — comes from overwatering and poor airflow.
proof: You raise a tray of seedlings from seed to healthy planted-out plants.
